questions.question: Choose the correct completion: 'The hot weather had a bad ___ on milk production.'
questions.rationale: Effect is the noun (a result); affect is the verb (to influence). 'Had a bad effect' - the noun slot needs effect. Remember: Action = affect (verb), End result = effect (noun).

questions.question: 'The new policy will ___ thousands of farmers.'
questions.rationale: The blank needs a verb (will + verb), so 'affect' (to influence) is correct. 'Effect' as a verb exists only in the special sense of 'to bring about' (effect change).

questions.question: Which sentence uses ITS/IT'S correctly?
options: The committee published its report yesterday.
The team changed it's captain mid-season.
The dog wagged it's tail happily.
questions.rationale: 'Its' (no apostrophe) is the possessive - the report belonging to the committee. 'It's' expands to 'it is/it has', which fits neither the possessive nor the 'Its a matter' error (should be 'It's a matter').

questions.question: The school ___ gave an inspiring speech, defending the ___ of fair play.
questions.rationale: The head of a school is the principal (your pal); a rule or belief is a principle. The 'principle is your pal' mnemonic fails here - only the person is the pal.

questions.question: The shop sells ___ : pens, envelopes and paper. Meanwhile, the ___ bicycle refused to move.
questions.rationale: Stationery (e for envelope) is writing material; stationary (a for 'at') means standing still. Both fill their own slot in this classic double-test.

questions.question: A word that is SPELLED the same but has different meanings, like 'bear' (animal) and 'bear' (to carry), is a:
questions.rationale: Homographs share spelling but differ in meaning (and sometimes sound, like tear/tear). Homophones share sound but differ in spelling (pair/pear).

questions.question: Which pair completes the sentence? 'The minister made an ___ to Shakespeare; the magician created the ___ of floating.'
questions.rationale: An allusion is an indirect reference; an illusion is a false image. Elusion (escaping) is the rare third twin and fits neither slot here.

questions.question: 'The judge must remain ___ in the case, even if he is personally ___ in cricket.'
questions.rationale: Disinterested means impartial - the judge's duty. Uninterested means bored - how he may feel about cricket. Swapping them is one of the commonest register errors in formal writing.

questions.question: There are ___ students in the corridor than yesterday, so we need ___ time to finish.
questions.rationale: Fewer goes with countable nouns (students); less with uncountable (time). The supermarket '10 items or less' sign is the standing joke of this rule.

questions.question: In 'Its too late too except there offer', how many homophone errors are there?
questions.rationale: The errors: Its -> It's ('it is' fits); the second too -> to (infinitive marker before 'accept'); except -> accept (to receive); there -> their (possessive). The first 'too' is correct - 'too late' means excessively late. Corrected sentence: 'It's too late to accept their offer.'
